# Scope

This notebook compares the signature-based clusters with a scalar copy number
measure, the fraction genome altered (FGA), in the clustering, survival, and
prediction analyses (Supplementary Figure 9). It uses the same tumors, saved
cluster fits, and train/test splits as notebooks `02`, `03`, and `04`.

| Step | Script | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FGA download | `code/scripts/fga_fetch.R` | `data/processed/fga_pancanatlas.csv` |
| Clustering | `code/scripts/fga_clustering.R` | `results/fraction_genome_altered/clustering_fga_*.csv` |
| Survival | `code/scripts/fga_survival.R` | `results/fraction_genome_altered/survival_cox.csv` |
| Prediction | `code/scripts/fga_prediction.R` | `results/cluster_prediction/fga_only/` |
| Supplementary Figure 9 | `code/scripts/supplementary_figure9.R` | `results/figures/Supplementary_Figure9.*` |

The clustering and survival analyses run in a few seconds and are rerun here.
The FGA download needs internet access, and the FGA-only classifiers are fitted
by `code/scripts/run_cluster_prediction.sh` (notebook `04`); this notebook
reads their results.

```{r packages}
library(ggplot2)
frameworks <- c("Drews", "Steele", "Tao")
```

# FGA data

FGA was taken from the TCGA PanCanAtlas studies in cBioPortal (sample attribute
`FRACTION_GENOME_ALTERED`): the fraction of the measured genome in segments with
an absolute segment mean of at least 0.2. One sample per patient was used: the
primary tumor or, when no primary sample was available, the metastatic sample
(365 patients, all skin cutaneous melanomas).

```{r fga-data}
fga_table <- read.csv("data/processed/fga_pancanatlas.csv")
fga <- setNames(fga_table$fga, fga_table$patient)
writeLines(readLines("data/processed/fga_pancanatlas_provenance.txt"))
summary(fga)
```

```{r coverage}
cl <- new.env(); load("data/processed/clustering_data.RData", envir = cl)
sv <- new.env(); load("data/processed/surv_data.RData", envir = sv)
fits <- c(Drews = "mc_drew_active_4", Steele = "mc_steele_active_4", Tao = "mc_tao_active_4")
survs <- c(Drews = "drew_f", Steele = "steele_f", Tao = "tao_f")
coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(frameworks, function(fw) {
  ids <- names(cl[[fits[fw]]]$classification)
  surv_ids <- rownames(sv[[survs[fw]]])
  share <- function(x) sprintf("%d / %d (%.1f%%)", sum(!is.na(fga[x])), length(x),
                               100 * mean(!is.na(fga[x])))
  data.frame(framework = fw, clustered_tumors = share(ids), survival = share(surv_ids))
}))
knitr::kable(coverage)
```

# Clustering

FGA by cluster, and the share of the variation in FGA explained by cluster
membership: overall (R²) and after accounting for cancer type (partial R² of
the cluster in `FGA ~ cancer_type + cluster`).

```{r clustering}
source("code/scripts/fga_clustering.R", local = new.env())
by_cluster <- read.csv("results/fraction_genome_altered/clustering_fga_by_cluster.csv")
variance <- read.csv("results/fraction_genome_altered/clustering_fga_variance.csv")
knitr::kable(by_cluster, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(variance, digits = 3)
```

# Survival

The cancer-type-stratified Cox models of Figure 7 (cluster, age, and purity),
fitted on the patients with an FGA value, without FGA (`figure7_fga_n`) and
with FGA as a penalized spline with 4 degrees of freedom (`with_fga_spline`).
A linear FGA term (`with_fga`) is given for comparison. Holm adjustment is
applied across the cluster coefficients of the six models of each set, as for
Figure 7. Patients without an FGA value are excluded from these models.

```{r survival}
source("code/scripts/fga_survival.R", local = new.env())
cox <- read.csv("results/fraction_genome_altered/survival_cox.csv")
cluster2 <- cox[cox$term == "cluster2" &
                  cox$model %in% c("figure7", "figure7_fga_n", "with_fga_spline", "with_fga"), ]
cluster2$hr_ci <- sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", cluster2$hr, cluster2$lower, cluster2$upper)
knitr::kable(cluster2[, c("framework", "endpoint", "model", "n", "events", "hr_ci", "p", "p_holm")],
             digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(unique(cox[, c("framework", "endpoint", "fga_nonlinearity_p")]), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Likelihood-ratio test of the spline against a linear FGA term")
```

# Prediction

Cluster 1 versus Cluster 2 classifiers from FGA alone, with the same patients,
splits, and tuning procedure as the multi-omic classifiers of notebook `04`.
Patients without an FGA value are kept, with the missing value passed to
XGBoost. Because the Cluster 1 F1 depends on class prevalence, the comparison
uses the balanced accuracy, the mean of the recall of Cluster 1 and Cluster 2.

```{r prediction}
models <- c(multiomic = "Multi-omic", multiomic_no_purity = "Multi-omic without purity",
            fga_only = "FGA only")
balanced <- function(x) (x$tp / (x$tp + x$fn) + x$tn / (x$tn + x$fp)) / 2
accuracy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(v) do.call(rbind, lapply(frameworks, function(fw) {
  m <- read.csv(file.path("results/cluster_prediction", v, fw, "split_metrics.csv"),
                colClasses = c(split_id = "character"))
  data.frame(framework = fw, model = models[[v]],
             split0_balanced_accuracy = balanced(m[m$split_id == "0", ]),
             median_balanced_accuracy = median(balanced(m[m$split_id != "0", ])))
}))))
knitr::kable(accuracy, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```
